To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conductivity of electroless Cu patterns on paper is affected by the type of paper, the plating time, the plating temperature, the feature geometry, the age of the catalyst patterns, and their interaction.
the electrical conductivity of Cu films electrolessly plated on paper is influenced predominantly by three factors: the plating temperature, the plating time, and the type of paper.
electroless copper plating of inkjet printed palladium catalyst on paper is affected by the type of paper used, plating time and temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the selective metallization of inkjet printed patterns on paper substrates.
the development of a process for the selective metallization of patterned paper surfaces.
the selective electroless metallization of paper-based inkjet printed patterns bearing a colloidal catalyst ink.

this work has shown that the electrical conductivity of the electroless copper films is dependent on the plating temperature, the plating time, and the paper substrate used.
the conductivity is influenced primarily by the type of paper, plating time, and plating temperature.
the conductivity of the Cu patterns is strongly dependent on the plating time and temperature, and to a lesser extent the paper type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrical conductivity of the electroless Cu films is a complex function of the plating conditions and the paper type.
the electrical conductivity of the electroless copper patterns is influenced by the paper, plating time and plating temperature.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the conductivity of electroless Cu plated on inkjet printed catalyst patterns on paper can be optimized by judicious choice of the process conditions.
the conductivity of electroless Cu plated onto paper substrates depends strongly on the plating temperature and time, and to a lesser degree on the plating bath and paper type.

the electroless Cu deposition process can be optimized for high electrical conductivity of the deposited films by careful control of plating temperature, time, and the type of paper on which the films are deposited.
